text: Project 1 was a DeFi protocol -- pool accounting, AMM math, economic security. Project 2 tests a different muscle: marketplace and escrow logic, plus a real indexing problem, since a raw node can't answer 'show me every active listing.'

Three layers. The contract, which you'll write in Lesson 9, handles listing, buying, and cancelling, with a royalty payout on sale. The indexing layer in Lesson 10 turns its events into queryable listings and sales history. The frontend in Lesson 11 connects a wallet and talks to both.

Scope is deliberately narrow so you can actually finish it. One ERC-721 collection, fixed-price listings, paid in ETH, and an approval-based listing -- the NFT stays in the seller's wallet until it sells. Royalties pay out automatically if the collection supports ERC-2981. Auctions, bundles, and ERC-20 payment are real features, but they're out of scope here on purpose.

Four flows carry the whole project. List: the seller approves the marketplace and sets a price. Buy: the buyer pays exactly that price, in one transaction that pays the royalty, pays the seller, and transfers the NFT together. Cancel: the seller can pull a listing any time. Discover: anyone can see what's listed, through the indexer, not the contract.

Before Lesson 9, scaffold the three project folders and write a one-paragraph scope statement for your own README. Next: designing the marketplace contract itself, with real, OpenZeppelin-backed Solidity.
